- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the early-period mean to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overpredict early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 2–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- After a strong upward spike in forecast, model often overshoots — apply a “cool-down” rule: subtract 1–2% from subsequent 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or declines.  
- If sentiment is consistently above 0.7 over 3–5 days, model tends to overcorrect — apply a 3–5% downward adjustment to final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- When sentiment is trending downward, model often fails to reflect mean reversion — add a 1–2% upward bias to mid-to-late forecast to capture rebound.  
- If sentiment is high but forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates momentum — increase forecast by 2–4% in first 3–5 days.
